newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.03 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.03 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.03 percent to close at 1.0435 per dollar in the commercial forex market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0435 to 1.0485 per dollar, dealers said.
The previous mini-band was set on Tuesday between 1.0430 and 1.0480 reais to the dollar.
The Central Bank repeated today Tuesday's move, lowering the mini-band just 0.05 percent, a level below market expectations of a 0.1 percent drop.
The 0.05 percent decline in the mini-band helped calm the market, which saw this move as another sign that the Central Bank is not speeding up the mini-band devaluations.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.43 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent.
Dealers said, however, players still remained concerned about the trade balance and how it could affect the current forex policy.
Brazil posted a $1.787 billion trade deficit on December and a total $5.539 billion trade deficit for 1996. Forecasts for the January trade deficit are around $1.0 billion.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0492 to the dollar, down 0.06 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.45 percent to end at 1.110 per dollar.
